message: No detected untrusted source handling: Data is fetched via imblearn's fetch_datasets without any checksum verification, signature validation, or pinned revision to authenticate the source.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The code performs only deduplication (drop_duplicates) but no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious inputs that would constitute a data poisoning defense.

No detected model integrity verification: The code only instantiates fresh model objects (DecisionTreeClassifier, RandomForestClassifier, SVC, Sequential) and never loads pretrained weights or a serialized model, so there is no integrity verification to observe.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no neural-cleanse, activation analysis, gradient anomaly detection, or any other backdoor/trigger defense in the training loop.
No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy library (Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD) is imported or applied during training.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial attack frameworks (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD, etc.) or robustness stress tests are present anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: Although KFold splits are used to separate train/test data, there is no signing or hashing of evaluation data, no truly held-out test set isolated before any pipeline decisions, and no independent auditing mechanism to prevent metric manipulation.

No detected input sanitization: The code only performs a label assertion (`assert np.all(np.unique(y) == np.array([0, 1]))`) and drops duplicates; there are no shape, range, or schema checks on the raw input features before they reach the model.

No detected output bounds checks: Model outputs are only passed through `np.around()` for rounding neural-network probabilities; there are no NaN guards, probability range checks, or sanity bounds on predictions before they are consumed.

No detected prompt injection defenses: The pipeline uses tabular classifiers (Random Forest, SVM, Decision Tree, shallow NN) and is not an LLM, so prompt-injection defenses are not applicable and none are present.
